title: Knowledge check: Understanding URLs, Domains, and Paths

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed for “Understanding URLs, Domains, and Paths”?
options: A complete substitute for server-side validation
A guarantee that every database write succeeds atomically
A feature that is always enabled without configuration
questions.explanation: The supplied Django curriculum lists “Domain names and hostnames” under lesson 26, “Understanding URLs, Domains, and Paths”. The lesson connects this item to the practical Django workflow for django architecture and http fundamentals.

questions.prompt: Which workflow best supports reliable work on “Understanding URLs, Domains, and Paths”?
options: Copy a production secret into the source file so every environment matches.
Publish an example before checking framework/version compatibility.
Use a documented small example, verify expected behavior, and test an invalid or boundary case.
Assume the browser is trusted and skip server-side checks.
questions.answer_key: Use a documented small example, verify expected behavior, and test an invalid or boundary case.
questions.explanation: Small reproducible examples, server-side validation where relevant, and explicit positive/negative checks help distinguish expected behavior from assumptions. Version, environment, and boundary cases should be documented.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most appropriate when applying “Understanding URLs, Domains, and Paths” in a real application?
options: Change multiple variables at once, then guess what fixed the issue.
Keep behavior explicit, validate at the correct boundary, and verify both success and failure paths.
Rely on a visual inspection alone.
Assume framework defaults replace application authorization rules.
questions.answer_key: Keep behavior explicit, validate at the correct boundary, and verify both success and failure paths.
questions.explanation: The lesson is part of Django Architecture and HTTP Fundamentals. Select the approach that supports correctness, safe handling of failures, and verifiable behavior; see the linked official documentation for version-specific details.
